text:
Leah: Heads-up — one of the corporate design partners asked for a short SLA + legal checklist before we send DP invites. They care about uptime, data residency/retention, telemetry access, and rollback policies. Can we list negotiables vs must-haves?
Mike_legal: Quick question — is an addendum to the DP agreement enough or do they want a full enterprise SOW? Also need to confirm KMS/HSM requirements.
Anya_solutions: They said 99.9% uptime and 30-day retention as their ideal. For beta, can we offer 99.5% with an option to upgrade? We should propose 90/30/opt-in retention tiers.
Sam_ops: From ops: 99.5% is realistic for pilot on hosted stacks. 99.9% would require reserved capacity. No credits during beta — just best-effort and incident transparency.
Raj_engineering: Tech note: we can provide aggregated telemetry dashboards and retention controls. We should avoid promising raw request export unless customer signs extra controls (PII handling). KV cache purge on request is feasible (72h).
Leah: @mike_legal can you draft a concise SLA addendum that keeps legal friction low? Also want a short safety clause: "no PII in prompts; we reserve right to pause traffic if safety signals detected."
Mike_legal: Will do. Drafting note — propose simple, non-enterprise language to avoid long signoff. Here's a starter snippet (for comment):
```
SLA: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide 99.5% monthly uptime for Redwood-hosted endpoints used during the Pilot. No fee credits are provided for pilot programs. Data: Customer data (requests, KV cache) is retained for 30 days by default. Upon written request, Redwood will delete KV cache and conversational logs within 72 hours. Telemetry: Aggregated metrics and latency dashboards are provided; raw request logs are only available with explicit consent and an approved data handling addendum. Fallbacks: If capacity or safety constraints occur, Redwood may route requests to a compatible model variant or temporarily restrict traffic with prior notice.
```
Anya_solutions: Add a short fallback line: "If routing to a variant, Redwood will notify the partner and provide a timeline to remediate." Keep it one sentence.
Sam_ops: Ops wants explicit scheduled maintenance windows + 72h advance notice for planned downtime. Also add an incident communication SLA (ack within 1 hour for Sev1).
Raj_engineering: For private/dedicated deployments we can hit 99.9% with committed capacity. Should call that out as an upgrade path in the addendum.
Leah: Also need an onboarding checklist in the invite: onboarding call, signed NDA (if not already), sample prompt set, eval set, POC contact, and expected acceptance criteria for launch.
DP-bot: Reminder: design-partner-invite-template v3 located at https://redwood.internal/docs/dp-invite-v3 — use it as base (template updated with beta terms). :robot_face:
Mike_legal: I'll circulate a 1-page SLA addendum + redlines by EOD. Will include a short data deletion paragraph and an opt-in for raw logs.
Sam_ops: I'll confirm planned maintenance cadence and propose standard windows (Tue/Wed 02:00-04:00 UTC) by tomorrow.
Raj_engineering: I'll draft the technical SOW piece for data deletion/kv purge and the upgrade path note for dedicated capacity.
Leah: Action items summary: Mike = draft addendum, Sam = confirm maintenance windows, Raj = technical SOW for deletion & upgrade path, Anya = prepare partner-facing talking points + fallback wording, Leah = update invite template with checklist. Aim to send invites next Tue. :calendar:
Anya_solutions: Sounds good. Quick ask — should we include a short sample eval (5 prompts) in the invite so partners can preview expected tests? I recommend yes.
Leah: Yes — include 5 sample prompts and the acceptance criteria (latency < 500ms p95, regression delta < 3% on quality eval).
Mike_legal: Uploading draft in #legal-review later. Ping me if you need quicker turnaround.
Leah: Thanks all — we'll reconvene if any partner pushes for enterprise terms. For now keep this tight and pact-friendly. :raised_hands:
